title: Sensitivity of polaron-molecule observables to MDR/GUP-like ultraviolet deformations at low energies via quantum computing
authors: Ezequiel Valero, Hugo Catala, Victor Ilisie, Germán Rodrigo
abstract: We show that impurity many-body observables can display enhanced sensitivity to ultraviolet deformations of generalized-uncertainty-principle and modified-dispersion-relation type at accessible energy scales. Using a deformed polaron-molecule Hamiltonian constructed to preserve the infrared sector, we quantify the impact of such deformations on spectral and Ramsey observables and implement the corresponding dynamics in a controlled quantum computing setting. We identify regimes near the polaron-molecule crossover where small ultraviolet deformations are strongly amplified, leading to experimentally resolvable changes in quasiparticle properties and spectral response. Our results establish a concrete sensitivity-based route to low-energy quantum-gravity phenomenology in a well-defined many-body platform and delimit the validity of the effective description. Furthermore, we report experimental validation on the QRed superconducting quantum processor (BSC-CNS).
summary: This work explores how hypothetical quantum gravity corrections, modeled by GUP/MDR terms, modify the behavior of polarons in fermionic baths. By analyzing spectral and coherence measurements using both theoretical calculations and superconducting quantum processors, the authors demonstrate that these deformations cause measurable shifts in energy spectra and alter the stability of molecular states near crossover points.
main_problem: The study investigates how ultraviolet (UV) deformations, inspired by Generalized Uncertainty Principles (GUP) or Modified Dispersion Relations (MDR), affect the low-energy many-body physics of a polaron interacting with a molecular bath.
main_result: These UV deformations enhance the sensitivity of measurable observables like spectral and Ramsey coherence signals near the polaron-molecule crossover, providing a concrete route to probe quantum gravity effects in ultracold atomic systems.
method: The authors employ both theoretical many-body techniques (e.g., ladder approximations, effective Hamiltonian construction) and advanced digital quantum simulation protocols on superconducting processors.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a polaron impurity interacting with a fermionic bath, described by an extended GUP-deformed Hubbard or polaron-molecule Hamiltonian. The physics spans the crossover between localized polaron states and delocalized molecular bound states.
key_observables: Spectral response (via FFT of Ramsey signal), coherence overlap $S(t)$, effective mass ($m^*$), and the shift/renormalization of resonance energies.
important_parameters: The GUP deformation parameter ($ eta$), low energy scales, and the polaron-molecule crossover regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis is phenomenological, treating UV deformations as controlled corrections to an effective low-energy Hamiltonian; quantum simulations rely on approximations like Trotter-Suzuki decomposition and error mitigation techniques.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the systematic shift of spectral peaks towards higher energies with increasing $ eta$, changes in Ramsey coherence contrast, and phase diagrams mapping out how the crossover point shifts based on the deformation strength.
paper_structure: The paper builds from theoretical derivations of GUP-corrected propagators and effective interactions to concrete quantum simulation protocols (Ramsey interferometry) used to measure these effects on superconducting hardware.
why_interesting: It bridges fundamental high-energy physics concepts (GUP/MDR) into a highly controllable, experimentally accessible platform (ultracold atoms/quantum simulators), providing testable predictions for deviations from standard condensed matter theory.

In the undeformed case, the stronger coupling to the molecular bath leads to a more pronounced suppression of the coherent response. Once the deformation is switched on, the time-domain signal develops a larger oscillation contrast and an additional node. This behaviour is consistent with the emergence of the GUP-induced next-nearest-neighbour hopping t′(β), together with the renormalisation of the effective impurity hopping ˜timp(m∗) and the dressed interaction ˜U GUP imp , all of which contribute to reshape the interferometric dynamics, executed on the QRed cluster.
